# Topic A — Correlation


## Q1 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** How strongly is car weight related to fuel economy (`mtcars`)?

```{r q1-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
plot(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars, pch = 16, xlab = "Weight (1000 lb)", ylab = "mpg")
r <- cor(mtcars$wt, mtcars$mpg)
round(r, 4)            # strong negative linear association
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------


## Q2 · L2 · Fill-in

**Goal:** Compute r from z-scores: r = Σ(zx · zy) / (n − 1).

```{r q2-l2}
x <- mtcars$wt; y <- mtcars$mpg; n <- length(x)
zx <- (x - mean(x)) / ___(x)
zy <- (y - ___(y)) / sd(y)
r_hand <- sum(___ * ___) / (n - 1)
round(c(r_hand, cor(x, y)), 4)
```

# Topic B — Least-squares Regression


## Q6 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Regress mpg on wt and interpret the slope.

```{r q6-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
fit <- lm(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars)
coef(fit)
plot(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars, pch = 16); abline(fit, col = "red", lwd = 2)
# Slope: each extra 1,000 lb is associated with about 5.34 fewer mpg on average.
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r q7-l2}
b1 <- cor(x, y) * ___(y) / ___(x)

round(c(b0 = b0, b1 = b1), 4)
```

# Topic C — Inference for the Slope & Prediction


## Q11 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Is the slope of mpg ~ wt different from 0?

```{r q11-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
s <- summary(fit)
s$coefficients                      # estimate, SE, t value, p-value
round(confint(fit, level = 0.95), 4)
# t = estimate / SE, df = n - 2
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------


## Q12 · L2 · Fill-in

**Goal:** Rebuild t and the 95% CI for the slope from its estimate and SE.

```{r q12-l2}
est <- summary(fit)$coefficients["wt", "___"]
se  <- summary(fit)$coefficients["wt", "___"]
t_stat <- est / se
df <- nrow(mtcars) - ___
tstar <- qt(___, df)
round(c(t = t_stat, lower = est - tstar * se, upper = est + tstar * se), 4)
```

# Topic D — Categorical & Multiple Regression


## Q16 · L1 · Reference

**Goal:** Regress mpg on transmission type (am as a factor).

```{r q16-l1, eval=TRUE}
# === Complete example — read and run ===
mtcars$trans <- factor(mtcars$am, labels = c("auto", "manual"))
fit_c <- lm(mpg ~ trans, data = mtcars)
coef(fit_c)
tapply(mtcars$mpg, mtcars$trans, mean)
# Intercept = mean of the baseline (auto); slope = manual - auto.
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------
